patient.name: Derek Simmons
patient.chiefComplaint: Right lower leg pain after ski fall, unable to bear weight

history.hpi: Patient was skiing at a resort when he caught an edge and twisted his right leg, resulting in immediate severe pain and inability to stand. Ski patrol arrived first and applied an improvised splint with a ski pole before EMS arrival. Patient denies head strike, loss of consciousness, or other injuries.
history.events: Ski patrol responded first, called EMS, and kept the patient still on the slope

scene.dispatch: 34-year-old male, ski injury, leg pain, unable to move, ski resort
scene.location: Mid-mountain ski run, patient on packed snow near a marked trail, ski patrol toboggan staged nearby
scene.safety: Ski patrol has closed the run above the patient; no additional hazards to crew
scene.bystanders: Ski patrol on scene, applied an improvised splint with a ski pole and jacket sleeve
visualCues: Obvious deformity to right lower leg below the knee
Boot removed by ski patrol, deformity visible through pant leg
No open wound or active bleeding visible

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 34-year-old male on packed snow with an obvious right lower leg deformity, splinted informally by ski patrol. He is alert, in severe pain, and denies other injuries.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact throughout; unable to fully assess right lower leg due to pain and deformity, sensation intact distally
otherFindings: Right lower leg pain 8/10, worse with any attempted movement
Obvious deformity below the right knee
Improvised ski-pole splint in place from ski patrol
Denies head strike, loss of consciousness, or other injuries
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It hurts so bad, please don't touch it!"

transitions.condition: Crew assesses pain and distal neurovascular status, splints the leg in the position found, establishes IV access, and administers weight-based fentanyl.

phases.name: IV obtained, fentanyl given
phases.description: Crew splints the deformed right lower leg, establishes IV access, and administers weight-based IV fentanyl for severe pain.
phases.triggerCondition: After confirming distal pulses, sensation, and movement, the crew splints the leg in the position found, establishes peripheral IV access, and administers fentanyl calculated to this patient's weight for his reported 8/10 pain.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses strong bilaterally, distal pulses present in right foot
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact distal to splint; strength intact elsewhere
otherFindings: Right lower leg splinted with vacuum splint
Pain decreased from 8/10 to 4/10 after fentanyl
Ice pack applied over splint, not directly on skin
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That's already helping a lot, thank you."

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess distal pulse, sensation, and movement before splinting
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Vascular status of extremity: Pallor, Pulse, Capillary refill and skin temperature. Neurologic status of extremity: Sensation to light touch, Distal movement of extremity
expectedActions.rationale: Establishes a neurovascular baseline before splinting to detect vascular compromise.

expectedActions.shortAction: Splint right lower leg in position found; apply ice pack, not directly on skin
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Use splints as appropriate to limit movement of suspected fracture. Apply ice/cool packs to limit swelling in suspected fractures or soft tissue injury, but do not apply ice directly to bare skin
expectedActions.rationale: Splinting in position found minimizes further tissue damage and pain.

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess pain using Numeric Rating Scale (patient >12 years old)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Greater than 12 years old: Self-report scale Numeric Rating Scale (NRS)
expectedActions.rationale: Establishes a baseline pain score to guide analgesic dosing and reassessment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 84 mcg IV (84 kg × 1 mcg/kg; max initial dose 100 mcg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Weight-based IV fentanyl targets severe pain without exceeding the max initial dose.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply capnography to monitor for early hypoventilation after opioid administration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Use of non-invasive capnography is an earlier predictor of hypoventilation than pulse oximetry if opioid medications are administered
expectedActions.rationale: Capnography detects hypoventilation before pulse oximetry would show desaturation.

transitions.if: Pain reassessed, repeat dose given, transport
transitions.condition: Five minutes after the initial fentanyl dose, pain remains at 4/10; crew reassesses vitals and administers a repeat fentanyl dose before transport.
Crew splints the fracture but withholds analgesia despite the patient's 8/10 pain and no identified contraindications.

phases.name: Pain reassessed, repeat dose given, transport
phases.description: Five minutes post-fentanyl, the patient's pain has decreased but is not fully controlled; crew reassesses vital signs and pain score, administers a second weight-based fentanyl dose per protocol, and transports in a position of comfort.
phases.triggerCondition: After reassessing vital signs and pain (now 4/10, still above target) and confirming no signs of hypoventilation or hypotension, the crew repeats a weight-based fentanyl dose five minutes after the first and transports the patient in a position of comfort.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact distal to splint
otherFindings: Splint remains well-secured, distal pulses intact
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel a lot better, thank you."

expectedActions.shortAction: Repeat fentanyl 84 mcg IV 5 min after first dose (84 kg × 1 mcg/kg; pain persists at 4/10)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If indicated based on pain assessment, and vital signs allow, repeat pain medication administration (excluding acetaminophen and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medicines) after 5 minutes of the previous dose
expectedActions.rationale: Persistent moderate pain after the first dose meets protocol criteria for a repeat dose.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport in position of comfort; reassess vitals and pain score en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Transport in position of comfort and reassess as indicated
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing reassessment confirms adequate analgesia without respiratory compromise.

phases.name: Fentanyl withheld despite severe pain
phases.description: The crew splints the leg but does not administer analgesia despite the patient's continued severe pain, resulting in ongoing tachycardia, hypertension, and patient distress during movement and transport.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew splints the deformed leg but withholds fentanyl despite an 8/10 pain score and no identified contraindications, leaving the patient's pain and physiologic stress response unmanaged.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses strong and bounding bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact distal to splint
otherFindings: Patient crying out with any movement
Increasingly anxious and uncooperative with packaging
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Please, it still hurts so bad, can't you give me something?!"

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize undertreated severe pain; administer fentanyl 84 mcg IV (84 kg × 1 mcg/kg; max 100 mcg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For Moderate to Severe pain, analgesics include: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Untreated severe pain drives the ongoing tachycardia and hypertension; weight-based fentanyl is indicated with no contraindications present.
